articles.title: The Expanded Scope of the Architect: Moving Windmills Innovation Center
articles.summary: What do architects do? This age-old question reveals the perennial dichotomy between two aspects of building–how to construct, and why to build. Despite its ancient origins and its name deriving from Ancient Greek, the profession is one that has transformed over the centuries. Its present-day form, usually dated to the Italian Renaissance , makes a distinction between the act of building and the intellectual and aesthetic decision-making behind it. However, we may be in the midst of another nascent transformation. The commissioning of architecture has historically remained separate from the pr

articles.title: SIMOSE Museum & Auberge / Shigeru Ban Architects
articles.summary: Located on a 4.6-hectare site facing the Seto Inland Sea, the facility consists of a museum, 10 villa-style accommodations, and a restaurant. In the center of the site, parallel to the coastline, a 180m-long, 8.5m-high mirrored glass wall has been erected to create a visual effect that doubles the landscape through reflection.

articles.title: In Conversation with Liu Jiakun, Dong Gong, and Luo Yujie: Small-Scale Timber Buildings—Why Build Them and How?
articles.summary: As timber architecture moves beyond traditional residential and rural settings to find new applications in urban regeneration, commercial spaces, public activities, and everyday life, we face new challenges and a growing need for "new architecture" that continues to evolve.

articles.title: Holland Grove / Blair Smith Architecture
articles.summary: Located in Melbourne , Holland Grove involved the comprehensive refurbishment of a two-level residence originally constructed in 2005, paired with the insertion of two new lightweight backyard pavilions. Designed by Blair Smith Architecture in collaboration with interior design studio Hecker Guthrie, the project re-evaluates the existing footprint to accommodate a blended family, prioritizing spatial expansion through quiet, landscape-focused additions.

articles.title: Renovation of the Core Area of TAFA Art Block / Mix Architecture
articles.summary: To the west of the Tianjin Academy of Fine Arts lies a century-old urban fabric. With the completion of the Tianjin Eye, the Haihe River's cultural and tourism flows converge at the Sancha Estuary, yet this nearby old town had remained a value depression dormant for two or three decades in the heart of the city. In 2022, the Hebei District Government of Tianjin and the Tianjin Academy of Fine Arts signed an agreement to jointly advance the campus development and the comprehensive enhancement of the surrounding area, giving rise to the TAFA Art Block urban renewal project. articles.title: Son Ferriol Health Centre / LaBoqueria
articles.summary: The project starts with a simple question: how can a building designed to care for people also care for its surroundings, its materials, and its own future?

articles.title: Ibitipoca House / Gávea Arquitetos
articles.summary: The Ibitipoca House is born from the logic of reuse. Faced with an old ruined building in the Serra do Ibitipoca, in Minas Gerais, the project begins with a disassembly operation that seeks to preserve, reconfigure, and re-inscribe the materials and traces of what already existed into the present. Instead of erasing the previous construction, the proposal transforms it into the material and conceptual origin of the new house.

articles.title: Lion Green Road by Mary Duggan Architects and RUFFARCHITECTS Wins RIBA Stirling Prize 2026
articles.summary: The RIBA Stirling Prize 2026 has been awarded to Lion Green Road , a housing development in Coulsdon, South London , designed by Mary Duggan Architects with RUFFARCHITECTS for Croydon Council. Comprising 157 homes across five residential blocks, the project combines privately owned and socially rented housing on a former car park. Presented annually by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) , the Stirling Prize recognizes a building considered to make a significant contribution to the evolution of architecture and the built environment. articles.title: Casa de Tierra / Walter Fernando Castañeda Luquerna
articles.summary: Located at an altitude of 3,012 meters above sea level, in a transitional landscape between Andean high-altitude forest and the páramo ecosystem, Casa de Tierra explores ways of inhabiting an environmentally sensitive territory through a strategy of minimal occupation and low environmental impact.

articles.title: Loungueira House / Pontoatelier
articles.summary: The project begins with the complete demolition of a fragile and poorly built structure, replaced by a compact house designed for the son and his family. The first gesture is to define the largest possible inhabitable footprint while respecting the required setbacks and preserving the existing guava tree. From this limit, the house is organized as a clear and continuous structure.

articles.title: Burden Museum & Gardens Welcome Center / Eskew Dumez Ripple
articles.summary: Conceived as a threshold, the Burden Museum & Gardens Welcome Center establishes a formal entry to the Burden Museum & Gardens campus through a series of simple, legible forms—architecture deliberately embedded in the landscape to frame, heighten, and ultimately reveal it. The new 6,500 SF Burden Museum & Gardens Welcome Center—with 3,000 SF of covered outdoor space—serves as the primary point of arrival to Burden Museum & Gardens and the broader LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens campus.

articles.title: Centre Pompidou Francilien — Fabrique de l’Art / PCA-STREAM
articles.summary: The Centre Pompidou Francilien – Fabrique de l'Art houses the reserve collections of two institutions. The building has two faces, reflecting the paradox at the heart of its brief. One side is a vault: a sealed monolith that admits only carefully controlled natural light into its workshops, so that two of the world's greatest modern art collections can be conserved and restored in the best conditions.

articles.title: Typological Drift: Emerging Cities in China
articles.summary: Typological Drift: Emerging Cities in China documents the impact of the Chinese culture on the development of city types in China in the past four decades, leading to surprising urban realities that often escape normative urban theories. Result of a decade of research by Shiqiao Li and Esther Lorenz in the two large city-regions in China, the Pearl River Delta and Yangtze River Delta, this book offers frameworks of understanding of China’s urban realities from within Chinese thought and language. articles.title: A Long View
articles.summary: A Long View explores the celebrated residential design of Bohlin Cywinski Jackson through the lens of fifteen private residences across the United States and Canada. With a curated selection of homes completed between 2016 and 2026, the book shares the evolution of BCJ’s work across a wider range of geographical regions and fresh material expressions, led by an emergent group of design voices within the practice who are carrying forward its ethos of humane, deeply collaborative design.
